whereToUse: Idrocrete KR 1000 may be used with any type of concrete when a reduction of permeability is required.
Idrocrete KR 1000 may be used to make concrete that is resistant to aggressive environments.
notFor: The specified exposure class of the concrete must always be respected and the product cannot be used to make up for poorly designed concrete.

To have guaranteed results, Idrocrete KR 1000 must only be used in concrete that has been correctly designed respecting two basic rules for the production of impermeable concrete, which are, a water/cement ratio of less than 0.5 and an adequate wet curing time.
Different dosage rates to those recommended above must be tested beforehand on concrete and, in all cases, only after consulting MAPEI Technical Services.

consumption.basis: Dosage by weight, per 100 kg of cementitious materials (DOSAGE section)
consumption.quote: The recommended dosage rate for Idrocrete KR 1000 is 1-3 kg/100 kg of cementitious materials.

consumption.basis: Dosage as a percentage of the weight of the binder (METHOD STATEMENT section)
consumption.value: 1-3% on the weight of the binder
consumption.quote: The crystallising admixture is added at a rate of 1-3% on the weight of the binder into the mixer unit along with the aggregates, cement, water and plasticising admixture and then mixed until it is completely blended.

mixing: Idrocrete KR 1000 is added to the concrete mix just like any other type of powder admixture. The product must be added in the concrete mixer or in the truck mixer together with all the other components (cement, admixtures and aggregates). Once Idrocrete KR 1000 has been added, we recommend extending the adequate mixing time so that the admixture is evenly blended throughout the mix.
packaging: Idrocrete KR 1000 is available in 20 kg and 4 kg water soluble bags.
storage: Idrocrete KR 1000 maintains its properties for at least 12 months if kept sealed in its original packaging, protected from moisture.
notes: The title is a rotated logo graphic that came out garbled in both text extractions ('Id KR', 'ete', 'cr 00'); titleAsPrinted is taken from the product name used throughout the body text, and the header also carries 'EN 934-2 T.9'. Dosage is printed twice and the two agree numerically: '1-3 kg/100 kg of cementitious materials' (DOSAGE) and '1-3% on the weight of the binder' (METHOD STATEMENT). The base is worded differently (cementitious materials vs binder) and the sheet gives no dosage per m3 of concrete, no guidance on where in the 1-3 range to dose, and no extra mixing time figure ('extending the adequate mixing time'). A calculator needs the cement/binder content of the mix as an input. The technical data table has only six rows. 'Alkali content ... ≤ 23' is copied as extracted; the label contains a subscript and the figure is worth a visual check against the PDF. The METHOD STATEMENT also lists properties for the CONCRETE made with the admixture, not for the product, so they are not in technicalData: density of concrete > 2300 kg/m3, strength class > C30/37, maximum water penetration < 30 mm (EN 12390-8 and DIN 1048), Darcy coefficient of permeability printed as '< 1x10-13 m/s' (exponent flattened in extraction). It also asks for a water/cement ratio of less than 0.5 and preferably type I and type II Portland cement. Body text adds: 'allows to close microcracks up to 0.4 mm'. whereToUse carries 6 of the 12 listed applications; the others are bridges, car parks, pipes and piles, marine structures, precast elements and 'white tanks'. The sheet has no 'do not use' list; notFor holds its stated conditions of use. The safety section says the product contains cement.
